decision_conditions: REPLACEMENT CONDITION 60 - Flood Management ReportNo above ground works (excluding Phase 0) that increase ground levels from existing site level and or reduce flood plain capacity shall take place until a site wide Flood Management Report is submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating:> Flood evacuation routes are provided and are either dry or in the "very low hazard level" (as defined by the Hazard table from the Research and Development Technical Report FD2320) for the 1 in 100 year plus climate change event. These details must include flood level, timings, and ground levels. This must be provided for parks and the public realm as well as buildings> Where flood evacuation is from a park site designated for flood storage, details on the return periods when flood storage is activated and flood hazard must also be provided in addition to the above> Details of flood resistant and resilient measures that are employed where appropriate. The information above may be demonstrated through supplementary flood modelling.Reason: To minimise flood risk in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy and Policies SI12 of the London Plan, Enfield's SFRA, DMD Policy 59, 60 & 62 and the NPPF

REPLACEMENT CONDITION 62 - Pymmes Brook Buffer ZonePrior to commencement of Phase 2, Block B, a scheme for the provision and management of a minimum 5 metre wide buffer zone alongside the Pymmes Brook as shown in drawing ref: 340-A-P-100-02 P01 approved as part of application reference 17/05006/RE4 shall be submitted to and agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Thereafter the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved scheme and any subsequent amendments shall be agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. The buffer zone scheme shall be free from built development including lighting, domestic gardens, hardstanding (e.g. footpaths) and formal landscaping; and could form a vital part of green infrastructure provision. The scheme shall include:1. Plans showing the extent and layout of the buffer zone - specifically where the proposed buffer zone will be wider than 8m to compensate for areas where 5m wide buffer was the widest possible width.2. Details of any proposed planting scheme. All new planting, including hydroseeding, within the buffer zone should be native species only, of UK provenance.3. Details demonstrating how the buffer zone will be protected and a detailed management plan for how the buffer zone will be managed/maintained over the longer term including a named body responsible for management.4. Details of any invasive non-native species present on site and how these will be managed in the longer term to prevent spread. Details showing a gradual transition between the artificial banked section of the Pymmes Brook within the PRS boundary and the re-naturalised section to the south of the PRS. Details of any proposed footpaths, fencing, lighting etc. The details shall include, but shall not be limited to the following: details demonstrating that the fencing will allow the free passage of mammals or that the fencing will be set back from the river bank (i.e. to the back edge of the buffer zone). Details demonstrating no artificial lightspill as a result of the development into the Pymmes Brook or its buffer zone. Light levels must be no higher than 2 lux within these areas.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance and design of Pymmes Brook and to ensure that the development contributes to improving the ecology and biodiversity of the area in accordance with paragraph 109 of the National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF), Policies 5.12 and 7.19 of the London Plan (2016), Policies CP28 and CP36 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and Policies DMD59 and DMD79 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

REPLACEMENT CONDITION 65 - Flood Store ManagementNo above ground works (excluding Phase 0) that increase ground levels from existing site level and or reduce flood plain capacity shall take place until a scheme for management of the flood storage areas including drainage mechanism, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority.The scheme should address as a minimum:> Full details on the flood storage area drainage mechanism which will form part of the forthcoming Naturalisation review must be submitted and approved by the Environment Agency. The mechanism for how the flood storage areas drain should be included in the next model submission.> Full details of any pipes or culverted sections between the flood storage areas, including size, depth and gradient.> Details of how any and all pipework or culverts that are utilised for the conveyance of flood water either into or subsequently out of flood storage area will be prevented from blocking in order to assure the flood storage areas are functioning to the full extent they are proposed.> Full details of how any and all pipework, culverts or outfalls that are utilised for the conveyance of flood water either into or subsequently out of flood storage area will be maintained for the lifetime of the development. This should include how they be replaced if required, frequency of inspection and who will be responsible for this maintenance regime.The scheme shall be fully implemented and subsequently maintained, in accordance with the scheme's timing/phasing arrangements, or within any other period as may subsequently be agreed, in writing, by the local planning authority.Reason:> To ensure that there are no detrimental impacts to flood storage or flood flow routes> To reduce the risk of flooding to the proposed development and future users.

REPLACEMENT CONDITION 15 - Planting, landscaping and public realm detailsPrior to the commencement of each area of public realm or communal amenity space within each Phase, except in the case of Phase 0 where details will be submitted prior to the commencement of Phase 1 (Block D), the following details of all landscaping, public realm and highway shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  The detailed specifications and design should be in line with the information included in the indicative Landscape Design Statement (10-12-2021 ), approved Landscape Drawings as set out in Condition 2.Details shall include:a. Open space and play provisionDetailed specifications and designs of the play spaces, including:- Details of surface materials and planting in each of the play spaces- Details of children's play equipment, including structures or play elementsb. Landscaping and plantingFinal selection of plant species, including their location, species and size/density, including:- Written specifications for operations associated with plant and grass establishment, and maintenance that are compliant with best practise;- details of how the landscaping and planting conforms with the Drainage Strategy (Preliminary Drainage Strategy (LD506-5122-WAL-XX-XX-RP-C-90-0013 P06 July 2022 and details required in accordance with Condition 30);- details of paving and hard surfacing materials- details of street furniture, including seating, planters, bollards- details of all signs and wayfinding elements- details of boundary treatments, including fencing materials, edging, plantersc. Highway worksDrawings and details of all highway works identified in the indicative Landscape Design Statement (10-12-2021), and approved General Arrangement Plans including paving, level changes, kerbs, traffic calming measures and associated landscaping and planting features, as aboved. Prior to the commencement of landscaping works, details of landscaping and planting that demonstrates a 10% Biodiversity Net Gain with the aim of achieving a 20.02% increase in habitat units, a 100% increase in hedgerow units and a 31.2% increase in river units as provided in the Biodiversity Net Gain Calculation December 2021, which used the Biodiversity Metric 3.0 calculation tool developed by Natural England.The site shall be landscaped strictly in accordance with the approved details in the first planting season after completion or first occupation of the development, whichever is the sooner.Reason: To ensure that the ecological value of the site is enhanced post development, and to comply with Policies CP30 and CP36 of the Core Strategy, Policies DMD37, DMD80 and DMD81 of the Development Management Document and Policies D4, D8, G4 and G5 of the London Plan.

REPLACEMENT CONDITION 38 - Circular Economy StatementPrior to commencement of each phase of development, a Circular Economy Statement prepared in satisfactory on London Plan Policy S1 7 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Circular Economy Statement must be consistent with the details of the Site Waste Management Plan, Operational Site Waste Management Plan and Construction Site Wate Management Plan. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure compliance with London Plan Policy SI 7 Reducing waste and supporting the circular economy.

REPLACEMENT CONDITION 16 - New TreesPrior to commencement of each area of public realm or communal amenity space (excluding Phase 0) a detailed tree planting strategy that includes, at minimum, the tree coverage shown in Phase 1B Planting Plans…shall be submitted with associated plans and standard planting details to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure all trees are planted with adequate conditions to meet maturity, support climate change adaptation, mitigate urban heat islands effects and support biodiversity in the long term.Informative:The tree planting strategy shall detail:o The key constraints and opportunities from the Soil Resource Plan and how tree planting is adapted accordingly;o The basis of tree planting proposals both aesthetically and how long-term growth and vitality will be supported;o That species are selected that will reach maturity and be in proportion to buildings and open space at maturity;o How trees will be incorporated into SUDS proposals and be complementary in design and function;o Using recognised calculations, how soil volumes will be maximised and matched to the proposed species and site layout so that sufficient water and nutrients will be available to all trees at maturity;o How subsurface engineering systems such as plastic crates or supports (e.g green blue urban, deep root) will be utilised, justified and minimised to ensure sustainable growth while minimising underground complexity and reliance on plastics;o How soil volumes in planting pits will be amalgamated appropriately to avoid undue competition between adjacent trees while enhancing shared soil space;o How tree planting pit dimensions and positioning of trees will enable balanced root growth into maturity;o Each tree pit dimensions below ground, maximum possible soil volume, proposed soil volume, and required soil volume for the species.Advisory: Reference documents include TDAG - Trees in Hard Landscapes: A Guide for Delivery (2014), Tree Species Selection for Green Infrastructure: A Guide for Specifiers (2018), BS 8545:2014 Trees: from nursery to independence in the landscape: Recommendations. Trowbridge and Bassuk - Trees in the Urban Landscape: Site Assessment, Design and Installation. J. Urban - Up by Roots: Healthy Soils and Trees in the Built Environment.

REPLACEMENT CONDITION 41 - LevelsThe development of any part of the above ground works (excluding Phase 0) shall not commence until plans detailing the existing and proposed ground levels including the levels of any proposed buildings, roads and/or hard surfaced areas, and evidence that proposed levels do not reduce flood plain capacity have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be constructed in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure that levels have regard to the level of surrounding development, gradients and surface water drainage.

REPLACEMENT CONDITION 49 - Meanwhile Use StrategyPrior to commencement of development (excluding Phase 0) a Meanwhile Use Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority with details of:i) Use;ii) Landscaping;iii) Management and Maintenance;iv) Security;v) Boundary Treatment; andvi) Access.The meanwhile plots shall be used, maintained and enclosed in accordance with the approved strategy.Reason: To safeguard the amenities of neighbouring residential occupiers and ensure a satisfactory appearance to the development in accordance with policy CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and DMD81 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2010).
